The ability of the second copy of Wide-Eyed Diver does not add to it's total lore because it was not in play when you played your second action so it's ability does not trigger.

q: I have a ready Alice - Growing Girl and Moana - Born Leader at the same location. If Moana quests while Alice is ready, will Alice be able to quest this turn?
a: No. Moana - Born Leader's ability Welcome to My Boat is mandatory and affects all other characters at the location she's at. Even if Alice - Growing Girl is ready when Moana quests, Alice won't be able to quest later this turn. Note that Alice still won't be able to quest this turn even if she moves to a different location or the location she and Moana are at is removed from play.

q: I control Cogsworth- Grandfather Clock and his Unwind ability is giving all of my other characters Resist +1. If I play a Mother Gothel- Withered and Wicked, how much damage will be on her?
a: 3 damage. Mother Gothel's ability does not count as damaging her so even if she has Resist she will still enter play with 3 damage counters on her.

q: My Mufasa- Betrayed Leader is banished and I use his The Sun Will Set ability. The card on top of my deck when the ability is used is an action card. When I return that card to the deck does it return face up or face down?
a: Face down. All cards in the deck are face down at all times unless otherwise specified.

q: I quest with my Mulan- Reflecting and use her Honor to the Ancestors ability. The card on the top of my deck is a copy of Be Prepared and I chose not to play that card. What happens to the card in this case?
a: The card is returned to the top of your deck. Even if the card is a song card as long as you choose not to play it then the card is returned to the top of your deck, face down.

q: If I have a character with Resist+1 in play when I play On Your Feet! Now! will that character be able to quest after I ready them?
a: No. On Your Feet! Now! affects all of your characters that are in play for each of its effects. First it will ready them and deal 1 damage to each of them. Those with Resist +1 will reduce that damage by 1 before any damage is dealt to them and receive no damage. All your characters will be unable to quest the rest of the turn, even if they were ready when On Your Feet! Now! was played and even if they didn't receive damage from it.

q: Can I choose the same character twice to receive the -1 strength from Painting the Roses Red?
a: No, you cannot. If you choose more than one character with the ability of Painting the Roses Red then they must be different characters.

q: If I use Perdita - Devoted Mother's ability Come Along, Children and play Madam Mim - Snake from my discard pile, do I still have to return a character to my hand from play or banish Madam Mim?
a: Yes. Perdita's ability Come Along, Children only plays a character without requiring you to play their ink cost. All abilities that apply when you play that character still apply.

q: I have a Peter Pan - Lost Boy Leader at The Queen's Castle - Mirror Chamber, which has 2 {L}. If I move Peter Pan to De Vil Manor - Cruella's Estate, which has 1 {L}, and then move him back to The Queen's Castle, can I use his I Came to Listen to the Stories ability to gain 2 lore?
a: No. You must use Peter Pan - Lost Boy Leader's ability I Came to Listen to the Stories the first time he moves to a location each turn. If he hasn't moved on your turn and you move him to De Vil Manor, you gain 1 lore. You can't use his I Came to Listen to the Stories ability again that turn.

q: I have a Prince John - Greediest of All in play and play a You Have Forgotten Me, causing my opponent to discard 2 cards. Can I choose to draw only 1 card with Prince John's I Sentence You ability?
a: No, you cannot. When choosing to draw with Prince John's I Sentence You ability you must draw equal to the number discarded. So in this example you would either draw 2 cards if you used the I Sentence You ability or 0 if you choose not to use it.

q: I have 10 lore and my opponent has 12 lore. If I quest with my Prince John - Phony King, who has 2 {L}, can I use his Collect Taxes ability to make my opponent lose 2 lore?
a: No. When a character quests, they immediately gain lore equal to their {L}. This means that in order to use Prince John - Phony King's ability Collect Taxes to have an opponent lose lore, they must have more lore than you after you've gained the 2 lore from Prince John's quest.

q: If an opposing character challenges a character during their owner's turn and is banished during the challenge can I ready my Queen of Hearts- Capricious Monarch using her Off With Their Heads! ability?
a: Yes, you can.

q: Three of my characters have 2 damage each on them. If my Rapunzel- Gifted Artist sings Hakuna Matata in that situation, how many cards can I draw with her Let Your Power Shine ability?
a: 3 cards. Rapunzel- Gifted Artist's ability triggers for each individual character of yours that has damage removed from them regardless of how much damage is removed from that character.

q: If the only characters my opponent controls have greater than 3 strength can I still use Ratigan-Very Large Mouse's This is My Kingdom ability to ready one of my characters?
a: Yes, you can. You will not be able to exert any characters using the ability but you can still do as much as you can of the ability.

I have 7 cards in my hand and Sheriff of Nottingham - Corrupt Official in play. I play A Whole New World, which makes me discard all my cards at the same time. How much damage will I be able to deal with the Sheriff's ability Taxes Should Hurt?
a: 7 damage. You can use Sheriff of Nottingham - Corrupt Official's ability Taxes Should Hurt once for each card you discard, even if you discard them at the same time. If you discard 7 cards due to the effect of A Whole New World, you may use Taxes Should Hurt up to 7 times.

q: If I banish a shifted Floodborn card in a challenge while I have a card that lets me gain 1 lore when I banish a character, how much lore do I gain?
a: No matter how many cards are in a shifted character's stack, they still count as a single character. Only the top card of a shifted character's stack is considered banished for the purpose of effects like this. Example: If you banish a shifted character with Simba - Rightful Heir, you still gain only 1 lore from his ability I Know What I Have to Do.

q: When I quest with Sisu- Divine Water Dragon can I choose not to use her I Trust You ability?
a: No, you cannot. Whenever you quest with Sisu- Divine Water Dragon you must look at the top two cards of your deck. You do not have to put one of the cards to your hand but regardless of whether you put a card in your hand or not any card you looked at and did not put in your hand must be placed on the bottom of your deck.

q: Can I use the A Silly Song ability of Sleepy's Flute even if I have not played a song this turn?
a: Yes, you can. In this instance you would exert Sleepy's Flute for the cost of the ability but since you have not played a song during this turn you do not gain a lore.

q: Can I choose a character with no damage on it for Sword in the Stone's ability?
a: Yes, you can. However the chosen character will not gain any strength.

q: When playing Teeth and Ambitions if I choose a copy of Cinderella- Singing Sword, which has Resist 2, as my character to deal 2 damage to, can I still deal 2 damage to an opposing character as well?
a: Yes, you can. Even in this example you can still deal 2 damage to an opposing character.

q: I have 2 copies of Jafar - Lamp Thief and 1 Genie - Supportive Friend in play. If I use the Good or Evil ability of The Lamp, what are my choices?
a: If you have a character named Jafar in play when you use the Good or Evil ability of The Lamp, you must draw 2 cards. You can't draw more cards even if you have other Jafar characters in play. If you have a character named Genie in play, you must return a chosen character with cost 4 or less to their player's hand. Neither is optional, and if you have both a character named Jafar and a character named Genie in play, you must do both.

q: Can I play The Most Diabolical Scheme if I do not control a villain character?
a: Yes, you can. However the first part of The Most Diabolical Scheme's ability is required to use the second part of the ability. So if you play The Most Diabolical Scheme without a villain character in play then you will not be able to banish an opposing character

q: I have a The Queen- Commanding Presence and a Flounder- Voice of Reason in play. My opponent has a Mickey Mouse- True Friend and a Maleficent- Sorceress. In this situation if I quest with my The Queen- Commanding Presence and use her Who is the Fairest? Ability, what characters can I choose for each part of her effect?
a: When using the Who is the Fairest? Ability of The Queen- Commanding Presence you must choose an opponent's character to receive -4 strength. This means that you can only choose either Mickey Mouse or Maleficent to receive -4 strength in this example. When using the second part of the Who is the Fairest? Ability you may choose any character to receive +4 strength. In this example you may choose Mickey Mouse, Maleficent, The Queen or Flounder to receive +4 strength. Note that you must choose a character for each part of the ability so you are not able to decrease the strength of a character and not increase the strength of a character.

q: Can I quest with The Queen- Peddler even though she has 0 lore?
a: Yes, you can. When you quest with a character that has 0 lore you will not gain any lore.

q: When naming a card for the Incredible Energy ability of The Sorcerer's Hat, what information do I need to say about the card?
a: When naming a card for the Incredible Energy ability of The Sorcerer's Hat, you don't need to declare the version name, even if the named card is a character or location.

q: If my only character with Bodyguard is at Tiana's Palace - Jazz Restaurant, can my opponent challenge any of my characters?
a: Yes. A challenging character must challenge an opposing character with Bodyguard if able, but the Night Out ability of Tiana's Palace makes characters there unable to be challenged. Therefore, challenging characters can challenge any character they'd normally be able to.

q: Challenger is additive, meaning you add up all numerical instances of it for a combined +N {S} gain. Example: If you have two of Tinker Bell - Peter Pan's Ally in play, each of them gives your Peter Pan characters Challenger +1, giving him a total of Challenger +2.
When can I play the additional song using Ursula - Deceiver of All's ability What a Deal?
a: When using the What a Deal ability of Ursula - Deceiver of All, you must play the song immediately after you played it the first time. You can't wait until later in the turn.

q: The only character in play is my Ursula - Deceiver of All, who currently has 1 damage. If I have Ursula sing Let the Storm Rage On, can I use her What a Deal ability to play it again?
a: Yes. When you play Let the Storm Rage On, if there's a character in play you can choose to deal 2 damage to, you must do so. Even if Let the Storm Rage on banishes your Ursula - Deceiver of All, you can still use her What a Deal ability. In this case you won't be able to deal 2 damage to a character, as there aren't any in play, but you still draw a card.

I currently have 10 characters and play a copy of Zero to Hero. In this case can I play a character from my hand that costs 5 ink for free using the ability of Zero to Hero?
a: Due to the effect of Zero to Hero you pay 10 less ink to play the next character you play. If that character costs equal to or less than 10 then you play it for free (you do not exert any ink to play it). Note that even in the above instance you may only reduce the cost of a single character. Even if you have 10 characters in play when you play Zero to hero you may not play 2 5 cost characters for free, just 1 character that costs 10 or less free or a character that costs more than 10 for 10 less than their printed cost.
